svg.aria-label: The HybriDock-Pep score network: three graphs, the noise-dependent cross-edge cutoff, the Clebsch-Gordan tensor-product layer, the growth of the hidden irreps over four layers, and the four output heads.
svg.text: Three graphs: receptor, peptide and cross
each residue linked to its 24 nearest neighbours (top_k = 24)
cross edges: peptide ↔ receptor within c(t)
Four contact types per cross edge
Cross-edge radius shrinks as the pose settles: c(t) = 40 Å + 3σ_tr(t)
edges kept for the cross graph: all peptide–receptor pairs closer than c(t)
h_i′ = BatchNorm( mean over j of TP( h_j ⊗ Y_l(r̂_ij) ; w(e_ij) ) ), l ≤ 2
Equivariance: Clebsch–Gordan coefficients couple the feature orders (l₁, l₂) to an output order l,
so rotating the input rotates every output tensor in the same way (Geiger & Smidt, 2022).
Messages run on three edge sets: intra-peptide, intra-receptor and cross (both directions).
Hidden representation grows over the four layers
ns = 48 scalar channels (0e, 0o) and nv = 10 vector channels (1o, 1e, each 3 dims).
No second-order terms. The receptor is not updated on the last layer.
Four score heads, the update step and the training objective
translation score: s_tr = f_tr(‖v‖, σ-emb) · (v/‖v‖) / σ_tr
rotation score: s_rot = f_rot(‖w‖, σ-emb) · (w/‖w‖) · κ(σ_rot)
v = first 1o + 1e vector, w = second 1o + 1e vector; κ is the SO(3) score norm
L = 0.25·L_tr + 0.25·L_rot + 0.25·L_bb + 0.25·L_sc (denoising score matching, one term per degree of freedom)
850 epochs · learning rate 1e-3 · batch 16 · moving average of weights 0.999 · about 7.56 million parameters
Source: RAPiDock training configuration (Zhao et al., 2025)
